notesStmt.note: This is one of several printed copies bearing the same set of minor, hand-written alterations and annotations. Whitman apparently created these to present as souvenirs. In the notes of his visits to Whitman on 30 September and 31 October 1889, Horace Traubel describes these "slip copies" of the poem, including the handwritten alterations. (See With Walt Whitman in Camden [Carbondale and Edwardsville: Southern Illinois University Press, 1982] 6:32, 204).
"Bravo, Paris Exposition!" was first published in Harper's Weekly on 28 September 1889 and reprinted, with a few changes in punctuation, in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: BRAVO, PARIS EXHIBITION Exposition!
lg.l: Add to your show, dear before you close it, France,

With all the rest, visible, concrete, temple, towers, goods, ma-
chinesmachines
and ores,

Our sentiment wafted from many million heart-throbs, ethereal
but solid,

(We grand-sons and great-grand-sons do not forget your grand-
sires,)

From fifty Nations and nebulous Nations, compacted, sent
over-sea to-day,
America's applause, love. memories and good-will.
